iran2026.title: US-Israeli strikes on Iran (scenario as on the evening of 27 February 2026)
iran2026.text: In June 2025, Israel and Iran fought a twelve-day air war. On 22 June 2025 the United States bombed Iran's nuclear sites at Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan; a ceasefire took effect on 24 June 2025. Iran's Supreme Leader is Ayatollah Ali Khamenei (born 1939); no successor has been publicly designated. On 11 February 2026, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu met President Trump at the White House. Assume the following: on 28 February 2026 the United States and Israel begin a large air and naval campaign against Iran, opening with strikes on Iran's leadership, air defences, missile and drone forces and navy. President Trump states his objectives: destroy Iran's missiles and missile industry, annihilate its navy, stop Iran's regional proxies, ensure Iran never obtains a nuclear weapon, and call on the Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) to lay down their arms and on Iranians to 'take over your government'. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through the Strait of Hormuz. On 27 February 2026, Brent crude costs about $72 per barrel.

iran2026_succession.title: Iran's leadership after the first strikes (1 March 2026)
iran2026_succession.text: On 28 February 2026 the United States and Israel began a large air campaign against Iran. On the morning of 1 March 2026, Iranian state broadcaster IRIB confirmed that Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed in a strike on his compound in Tehran on 28 February, and announced 40 days of mourning. Under Iran's constitution, the Assembly of Experts chooses a new Supreme Leader. Candidates discussed in the past include senior clerics and Khamenei's son Mojtaba Khamenei; a hereditary succession has often been described as controversial because the 1979 revolution overthrew a monarchy. Strikes are continuing.

twelveday2025.title: Israel strikes Iran (13 June 2025)
twelveday2025.text: In the early hours of 13 June 2025, Israel attacked dozens of Iranian nuclear facilities, military bases and other installations and killed several senior military commanders and nuclear scientists. Iran has promised retaliation. The United States had been negotiating with Iran about its nuclear programme; President Trump has said he prefers a deal but that Iran must not get a nuclear weapon. Iran's most protected enrichment site, Fordow, is built deep inside a mountain; only the United States has bombs designed to reach such sites.

indiapak2025.title: India strikes Pakistan (7 May 2025)
indiapak2025.text: On 22 April 2025, an attack near Pahalgam in Indian-administered Kashmir killed 26 civilians. India blamed Pakistan-based militants; Pakistan denied involvement. On 7 May 2025, India launched missile strikes on targets in Pakistan and Pakistani-administered Kashmir ('Operation Sindoor'). Pakistan says it shot down Indian aircraft and has vowed to respond. Both countries have nuclear weapons.

gaza2025.title: Trump's Gaza peace plan (29 September 2025)
gaza2025.text: On 29 September 2025, President Trump announced a 20-point plan to end the war in Gaza, with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu at his side. It foresees a ceasefire, the release of all hostages held in Gaza within 72 hours of Israel accepting the deal, the release of Palestinian prisoners, the disarmament of Hamas, an international stabilisation force and a transitional administration. Hamas has not yet responded. About 20 of the hostages are believed to be alive.

ukraine2025.title: Trump-Putin summit in Alaska (15 August 2025)
ukraine2025.text: On 15 August 2025, Presidents Trump and Putin met in Anchorage, Alaska, to discuss the war in Ukraine. Before the meeting, Trump said he expected at least a ceasefire. Ukraine's President Zelenskyy was not invited. Since March 2025, Ukraine has offered an unconditional ceasefire; Russia has insisted on its conditions, including Ukraine withdrawing from the Donbas region. The summit ended without an announced agreement.

venezuela2025.title: US pressure on Venezuela (1 December 2025)
venezuela2025.text: Since August 2025, the United States has deployed thousands of troops and several warships to the Caribbean; the aircraft carrier USS Gerald R. Ford arrived in the area on 16 November 2025. Since September 2025, US forces have struck boats that the US says carried drugs from Venezuela, killing more than 80 people. On 24 November 2025, the US designated the 'Cartel de los Soles', which it says is led by President Nicolas Maduro, a foreign terrorist organisation. The US offers a $50 million reward for information leading to Maduro's arrest. On 27 November 2025, President Trump told US troops: 'You probably noticed that people aren't wanting to be delivering by sea, and we'll be starting to stop them by land also. The land is easier, but that's going to start very soon.'
